mainTopic: Dividing an inheritance, and the limits of agency for a sin
overview: The גמרא first settles two rulings of רב נחמן about orphans dividing property. A value mistake of a sixth cancels the division, and without such a mistake the orphans can only complain about which plots they got. רב נחמן then rules that brothers who divide an inheritance are like buyers, so the usual sixth-rules of אונאה apply. רבא adds limits to this. A brother who sent a שליח can undo even a small loss. Brothers who chose a court appraisal cannot undo even a big mistake, which matches רבן שמעון בן גמליאל in a משנה. Returning the overcharge applies only to movable things, but land divided by measurement is corrected for any error, as רבה teaches. The גמרא then turns to שליחות and explains, from the משנה about sending fire, that אין שליח לדבר עבירה. מעילה is an exception learned from תרומה. Together with שליחות יד, whose source is 'על כל דבר פשע' according to בית הלל, the two are 'two verses that come as one' and do not teach a general rule. The amud ends by asking how this works for בית שמאי, and that question continues on the next amud.

steps.title: One ruling is where the court erred, the other where it did not
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא resolves the clash between רב נחמן's two rulings about orphans' division. In one case the court made a value mistake, and in the other it did not.
steps.simpleTranslation: This case is where they made a mistake. That case is where they did not make a mistake.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is answering a contradiction raised just before this point between two rulings of רב נחמן about orphans who divided their father's property through the court. It says the two rulings deal with different cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Where רב נחמן said the division is void, the court misjudged the value by a sixth. Where he said the orphans cannot protest later, there was no such value mistake. Once the cases are told apart, the two rulings no longer clash.

keyTerms.meaning: this one / that one (pointing to one of two cases)
they made a mistake (here, in valuing the property)

phrases.english: This one is where they erred,
phrases.notes: This means the ruling that the division is void. The court misjudged the value by a sixth.

phrases.english: that one is where they did not err.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא – דִּטְעוֹ, הָא – דְּלָא טְעוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised just before this point between רב נחמן's two rulings
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): each ruling applies to a different situation
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two rulings of רב נחמן seemed to contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: The division is void when the court erred by a sixth. The orphans cannot protest when there was no error.

steps.title: If there was no mistake, what could the orphans protest about?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the answer. If the court made no mistake, what is left for the orphans to protest about later?
steps.simpleTranslation: If they did not make a mistake, what does it mean that they can protest?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer it just gave. If the case with no mistake is the one where protest is discussed, what would the orphans even be complaining about?
steps.deeperAnalysis: A statement had spoken of orphans being able to protest later. If the values were correct, there seems to be no grounds for any protest. So the case without a mistake seems to leave nothing to object to.

phrases.english: If they did not err,
what is meant by "they can protest"?
phrases.notes: This goes back to the earlier ruling that the orphans can protest once they grow up.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי דְּלָא טְעוֹ, מַאי יְכוֹלִים לְמַחוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the case split given in step 1
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the no-mistake case is the one where protest is discussed
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the values were right, there seems to be nothing for the orphans to protest about.

steps.title: The protest is about locations, not value
steps.stepSummary: The orphans can object to which plots they received, even if every share was worth the right amount.
steps.simpleTranslation: They can protest about the locations.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The orphans' complaint is about where their share is, not about how much it is worth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even when every share has the correct value, an orphan may prefer land in a different spot, for example next to his other fields. That is the kind of protest meant here. It is not a claim of being cheated in value.
steps.whatToRemember: With orphans' division through the court: a value mistake of a sixth cancels it, and with no value mistake the only possible complaint is about which plots each one got.

phrases.english: They can protest about the directions.
phrases.notes: Meaning which side or location of the property each orphan received, not its value.

steps.triggerLanguage: יְכוֹלִים לְמַחוֹת בְּרוּחוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 2
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining what kind of protest is meant
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Protest must mean a claim about value.
steps.terutzMaskana: The protest is about the location of the plots, not their value.

steps.title: Brothers who divide an inheritance are like buyers
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן rules that brothers who split an inheritance follow the regular rules of overcharging in a sale.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: Brothers who divided an inheritance are like buyers from each other. If the mistake is less than a sixth, the deal stands. If it is more than a sixth, the deal is cancelled. If it is exactly a sixth, the deal stands and the one who got extra pays back the difference.
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching begins. רב נחמן says that dividing an inheritance between brothers works like a sale between them, so the usual rules of אונאה apply.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each brother is treated as if he bought his share from the others. So a small mistake under a sixth is forgiven, and a mistake of exactly a sixth must be paid back. A mistake over a sixth cancels the whole division.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the basic rule for inheritance divisions, and רבא's next two statements are limits on it.

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman said:
Brothers who divided are like buyers.
Less than a sixth: the transaction is acquired.
More than a sixth: the transaction is void.
Exactly a sixth: he acquires, and returns the overcharge.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן: הָאַחִין שֶׁחָלְקוּ הֲרֵי הֵן כְּלָקוֹחוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new teaching about dividing an inheritance
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An inheritance division follows the rules of אונאה: under a sixth it stands, exactly a sixth it stands and the extra is returned, over a sixth it is void.

steps.title: A brother who sent an agent can undo even a small loss
steps.stepSummary: רבא limits the 'less than a sixth' rule. If a brother sent a שליח who accepted a losing share, the brother can say the שליח had no authority to make him lose.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: When we said that under a sixth the deal stands, that is only when the brother did not send an agent. But if he sent an agent, he can say: I sent you to help me, not to hurt me.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא adds the first limit to רב נחמן's rule. The 'small mistake is forgiven' rule does not apply when a שליח made the division.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person who divides for himself accepts small mistakes. A שליח only has the power his sender gave him, and that power was to benefit the sender. So when the שליח accepts even a small loss, he acted outside his job, and the division does not bind the sender.

keyTerms.meaning: he appointed him as an agent

steps.confusionAlert: This limit applies only to the brother who sent the שליח and got less. רבא does not say the sixth-rules disappear for everyone.

phrases.english: Rava said:
That which we said, "less than a sixth, the transaction is acquired" —

phrases.aramaic: לָא אֲמַרַן אֶלָּא דְּלָא שַׁוְּיֵהּ שָׁלִיחַ,
phrases.english: we said it only where he did not appoint an agent,
but if he appointed an agent, he can say:
I sent you to benefit me, and not to harm me.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: הָא דַּאֲמַרַן ״פָּחוֹת מִשְּׁתוּת – נִקְנֶה מִקָּח״ – לָא אֲמַרַן אֶלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the first part of רב נחמן's rule
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When a שליח makes the division, even a loss of less than a sixth can be undone by the sender, because the שליח was sent only to benefit him.

steps.title: Dividing by a court appraisal stands even with a big mistake
steps.stepSummary: רבא limits the 'more than a sixth' rule. If the brother had asked to divide by the court's appraisal, the division stands even when the court's values were off by more than a sixth.
steps.simpleTranslation: And when we said that over a sixth the deal is cancelled, that is only when he did not say, 'Let us divide by the court's appraisal.' But if he said, 'Let us divide by the court's appraisal,' the sale stands.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a second limit to רב נחמן's rule. This time it is about the 'more than a sixth cancels it' part.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a big mistake cancels the division. But a brother who chose to rely on the court's appraisal accepted that appraisal as final. So he cannot cancel the division later, even over a large mistake.

phrases.english: And that which we said, "more than a sixth, the transaction is void" —
we said it only where he did not say:
"Let us divide by the court's appraisal,"
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets and some the word in square brackets. Both mean "let us divide."

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל אָמַר נִפְלוֹג בְּשׁוּמָא דְּבֵי דִינָא –
phrases.english: but if he said, "Let us divide by the court's appraisal" —
their sale stands,

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא דַּאֲמַרַן ״יָתֵר מִשְּׁתוּת – בָּטֵל מִקָּח״ – לָא אֲמַרַן אֶלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the second part of רב נחמן's rule, alongside step 5
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the brothers agreed to divide by the court's appraisal, the division stands even with a mistake of more than a sixth.

steps.title: Support from the משנה about a court's appraisal sale
steps.stepSummary: רבא backs up his second limit with a משנה. There, רבן שמעון בן גמליאל rules that a sale based on the judges' appraisal stands even when it is off by a sixth.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: When judges appraised something and were a sixth too low or a sixth too high, their sale is cancelled. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: Their sale stands.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא brings a source for his ruling. A משנה records a disagreement about whether a sale set by a court's appraisal can be cancelled for a mistake.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion in the משנה (the תנא קמא) treats a court's appraisal like any sale, so a sixth-sized mistake cancels it. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל holds the sale stands, because a court's appraisal carries its own authority. רבא's ruling that dividing by court appraisal stands matches רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's view.
steps.whatToRemember: Brothers who divide are like buyers and follow the sixth-rules (רב נחמן). רבא's first two limits: a brother who sent a שליח can undo even a small loss, and brothers who chose a court appraisal cannot undo even a big mistake. רבא adds a third limit, about land, in the next steps.
steps.confusionAlert: Both opinions come from the משנה. רבא's ruling matches רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, not the first opinion.

phrases.english: as we learned:
The judges' appraisal, where they decreased by a sixth
or added a sixth: their sale is void.

phrases.aramaic: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר: מִכְרָן קַיָּים.
phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says: Their sale stands.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for רבא's ruling in step 6
steps.raayaObject: רבא's ruling that a division based on a court appraisal stands even with a large mistake
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in כתובות, where רבן שמעון בן גמליאל holds that a sale based on the judges' appraisal stands

steps.title: The sixth rule applies only to movable property
steps.stepSummary: רבא limits the rule 'exactly a sixth: the deal stands and the extra is returned' to movable things. For land there is no אונאה at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: What we said, that with a mistake of a sixth the brother keeps his share but pays back the extra, applies only to movable things. With land, there is no overcharging.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא adds another limit to the brothers' division rule. The overcharging rules only cover movable property, not land.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With movable things, an error of exactly a sixth means the deal stands but the difference is returned. Land is a special exception: the Torah's overcharging rules do not apply to it. So if brothers split land by value and one share came out a sixth more valuable, the brother who got more does not pay back the difference.

keyTerms.meaning: One sixth, the amount of error that counts as overcharging
The overcharging rules do not apply to land

phrases.english: And that which we said: 'A sixth: he acquired, and he returns the overcharge'
we only said it about movable property,
but with land, there is no overcharging for land.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא דַּאֲמַרַן ״שְׁתוּת – קָנָה, וּמַחְזִיר אוֹנָאָה״ – לָא אֲמַרַן אֶלָּא בְּמִטַּלְטְלֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבא's series of limits on רב נחמן's rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The sixth-overcharge rule for dividing brothers applies only to movable property, because there is no אונאה for land.

steps.title: Land divided by measurement is different
steps.stepSummary: The 'no overcharging for land' rule only protects a division made by value. If the brothers divided by measuring and measured wrong, the mistake does not stand.
steps.simpleTranslation: And with land, we only said there is no overcharging when they divided by value. But if they divided by measurement, that rule does not apply.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא narrows the land rule itself. 'No overcharging for land' only helps when the division was based on value.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Dividing by value means each brother takes a plot judged to be worth the same. Then a mistake in price is ignored for land. Dividing by measure means they agreed on equal sizes. A wrong measurement is not a pricing issue at all, so the land exception does not cover it.

phrases.english: And with land, we did not say this
except where they divided by value,
but if they divided by measurement, no,
phrases.notes: He means that here the 'no overcharging for land' rule does not protect the mistake.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבִמְקַרְקְעֵי לָא אֲמַרַן, אֶלָּא דִּפְלוּג בְּעִילּוּיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the land exception just stated in Step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The rule that there is no overcharging for land applies only to a division by value, not to a division by measurement.

steps.title: Support from רבה about measured items
steps.stepSummary: This follows רבה, who says that anything sold by measure, weight or number goes back even if the error was smaller than a sixth.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is like רבה, who said: anything sold by measure, weight, or count can be corrected, even if the mistake was less than the overcharging amount.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא backs up the measurement limit from Step 9 by pointing to a rule of רבה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה teaches that when something is sold by an exact amount, any shortfall is simply a mistake and must be fixed, however small. So a division of land by measurement works the same way. A wrong measurement gets corrected, and the land exception does not apply.

keyTerms.meaning: The אמורא whose rule is cited here (not to be confused with רבא)
Goes back, the error is corrected

steps.confusionAlert: רבה (with a ה) and רבא (with an א) are two different אמוראים. Here רבא is the one speaking, and he is relying on רבה.

phrases.english: In accordance with Rabba.
As Rabba said:
Anything that goes by measure, by weight, or by number,

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ פָּחוֹת מִכְּדֵי אוֹנָאָה – נָמֵי חוֹזֵר.
phrases.english: even if it is less than the amount of overcharging, it still goes back.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּדְרַבָּה. דְּאָמַר רַבָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source behind the measurement limit in Step 9.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that a division of land by measurement is corrected despite the land exception.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבה's rule that any measured, weighed or counted item is corrected even for an error smaller than a sixth.
steps.whatToRemember: Brothers' division: movable items follow the sixth rule. Land divided by value has no overcharging. Land divided by measure gets corrected for any error, as רבה teaches.

steps.title: Fire sent with a competent messenger
steps.stepSummary: A משנה says that if someone sends fire with a competent person, only the messenger is liable. The גמרא asks: why not say שלוחו של אדם כמותו and hold the sender liable?
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned: if someone sends fire with a deaf-mute, a mentally incompetent person, or a minor, he is exempt in human court but liable in Heaven's court. If he sent it with a competent person, the competent person is liable. But why? A person's agent should count like himself!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the topic of שליחות. It quotes a משנה and then challenges it with the basic rule that an agent stands in for the sender.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If agency always worked, the sender of a competent messenger should be the one liable for the fire. Yet the משנה puts the liability on the messenger alone. So the משנה seems to clash with שלוחו של אדם כמותו.

keyTerms.meaning: A deaf-mute, a mentally incompetent person, and a minor: people not legally responsible
A person's agent is like himself

phrases.english: And that which we learned in a Mishnah:
One who sends fire
in the hands of a deaf-mute, a mentally incompetent person, or a minor
is exempt by human law,
but liable by the laws of Heaven.
If he sent it with a competent person, the competent person is liable.
But why?
Let us say: a person's agent is like himself!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא דִּתְנַן: הַשּׁוֹלֵחַ אֶת הַבְּעֵירָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the inheritance topic and opens a new discussion about the limits of שליחות.
steps.kashyaTarget: The general rule שלוחו של אדם כמותו.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If an agent is like the sender, the sender of a competent messenger should be liable, yet the משנה makes only the messenger liable.

steps.title: No agency for a sin
steps.stepSummary: The answer is that the fire case is different, because there is no שליח for a sin. The messenger should have listened to ה׳ rather than to the sender.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is different there, because there is no agency for doing a sin. As we say: if the Master and the student say different things, whose words do we listen to?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by saying agency does not work when the mission is a sin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The messenger was told by the Torah not to do harm, and by the sender to do it. He should have obeyed ה׳. Since he chose to sin anyway, the act is his own, and the sender is not liable through him.

keyTerms.meaning: There is no agency for a sin
The words of the Master (ה׳) versus the words of the student (a person)

phrases.english: It is different there,
because there is no agent for a sin.
As we say:
The words of the Master and the words of the student:
phrases.notes: The Master is ה׳, and the student is the person who sent him.

phrases.english: whose words do we listen to?

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁאנֵי הָתָם דְּאֵין שָׁלִיחַ לִדְבַר עֲבֵירָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the fire משנה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the case: agency is limited when the mission is a sin.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Agency always makes the sender responsible.
steps.terutzMaskana: When the mission is a sin, the messenger should have obeyed ה׳, so the act is his alone.
steps.whyThisMatters: אין שליח לדבר עבירה is one of the major limits on שליחות throughout ש״ס, and it is tested right away in the next step.

steps.title: Misusing הקדש through an agent
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says that when a שליח carries out the owner's mission with הקדש, the owner is guilty of מעילה. That seems to contradict אין שליח לדבר עבירה.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in a ברייתא: if the agent did not do what he was sent to do, the agent misused הקדש. If he did his mission, the owner misused it. So when he did the owner's mission, the owner is guilty. Why? We should say there is no agency for a sin!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer from Step 12 with a ברייתא where agency does seem to work for a sin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מעילה, misusing holy property, is a sin. Yet the ברייתא makes the owner guilty when his agent follows instructions, which means the agency worked. That clashes with the rule we just used, that there is no agency for a sin.

keyTerms.meaning: The owner, the one who sent the agent
His mission, what he was sent to do

phrases.english: And that which was taught in a Baraita:

phrases.aramaic: שָׁלִיחַ שֶׁלֹּא עָשָׂה שְׁלִיחוּתוֹ – שָׁלִיחַ מָעַל,
phrases.english: An agent who did not do his mission: the agent has misused holy property,
if he did his mission, the owner has misused it.
When he did the owner's mission,
the owner, in any event, has misused it.
Why?
Let us say: there is no agent for a sin!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָדְתַנְיָא: שָׁלִיחַ שֶׁלֹּא עָשָׂה שְׁלִיחוּתוֹ – שָׁלִיחַ מָעַל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer given in Step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule אין שליח לדבר עבירה used to explain the fire משנה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: מעילה is a sin, yet the ברייתא makes the owner guilty through his agent, so agency for a sin seems to work.

steps.title: מעילה is special because it is learned from תרומה
steps.stepSummary: מעילה is different. A גזירה שוה of 'חטא' 'חטא' links it to תרומה, where a שליח can act for you, so a שליח works for מעילה too.
steps.simpleTranslation: מעילה is different, because it is learned from the word 'sin' here and the word 'sin' by תרומה. Just as you can make a שליח for תרומה, you can also make a שליח for מעילה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 13. מעילה is an exception to the rule of אין שליח לדבר עבירה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'חטא' appears both by מעילה and by תרומה, and this links the two. A person can appoint a שליח for תרומה, so the same is true for מעילה. The Torah itself creates this exception, so the owner is liable even though a sin is involved.

keyTerms.meaning: It is different. The case is an exception.
Improper use of הקדש (property that belongs to the בית המקדש)
The word 'sin' appears in both places. This links the two topics in a גזירה שוה.
The portion of produce given to a כהן

phrases.english: Misuse of sacred property is different,
since it is learned from 'sin' and 'sin' by terumah:
phrases.notes: The two פסוקים are ויקרא 5:15 (about מעילה) and ויקרא 22:9 (about תרומה), and both use the word 'sin'.

phrases.english: just as with terumah one can appoint an agent,
so too with misuse one can appoint an agent.

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁאנֵי מְעִילָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in Step 13
steps.terutzResolutionType: Special exception learned from a גזירה שוה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: מעילה seemed to show that a שליח works even for a sin
steps.terutzMaskana: מעילה is a special exception taught by the Torah through its link to תרומה

steps.title: Why not learn a general rule from מעילה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: if a שליח works for מעילה, let us learn from it that a שליח works for every sin.
steps.simpleTranslation: So let us learn from it (that a שליח works for other sins too)!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer it just gave. If the Torah shows that a שליח works for מעילה, why not make that the rule everywhere?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally when the Torah teaches something in one case, we can apply it to similar cases. So the exception of מעילה might seem like a model for all sins. That would undo the rule of אין שליח לדבר עבירה.

keyTerms.meaning: There is no agent for a sin. The rule that this challenge threatens.

phrases.english: And let us learn from it!
phrases.notes: He means: learn from מעילה that a שליח works for any sin.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְנֵילַף מִינַּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer in Step 14 by trying to generalize it
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that מעילה is only a limited exception
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A rule the Torah teaches in one place should be applied to other cases as well

steps.title: Two verses that teach the same thing do not teach beyond themselves
steps.stepSummary: We can't generalize, because both מעילה and שליחות יד teach that a שליח works. When two verses teach the same thing, we do not learn from them to other cases.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because מעילה and שליחות יד are two verses that teach the same thing, and any two verses that teach the same thing do not teach (to other cases).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers why we cannot learn a general rule from מעילה. A second case, שליחות יד, teaches the same idea.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a שליח worked for every sin, the Torah would only need to say it once. Since the Torah had to say it twice (by מעילה and by שליחות יד), these must be special exceptions. So the general rule of אין שליח לדבר עבירה stays in place.

keyTerms.meaning: When a שומר takes the item he is guarding and uses it for himself
Two verses that come to teach the same idea
They do not teach (to other cases)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think that two verses make a rule stronger! Here the opposite is true. Because the Torah had to repeat it, we learn it is only for those two cases.

phrases.english: Because misuse and misappropriation of a deposit
are two verses that come as one,
and any two verses that come as one
do not teach.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשּׁוּם דְּהָוֵי מְעִילָה וּשְׁלִיחוּת יָד שְׁנֵי כְּתוּבִים הַבָּאִים כְּאֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 15
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rule of interpretation that blocks generalizing
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We might learn from מעילה that a שליח works for every sin
steps.terutzMaskana: מעילה and שליחות יד are two verses teaching the same thing, so they stay limited to themselves
steps.whyThisMatters: This is why the rule of אין שליח לדבר עבירה survives even though there are two cases where a שליח does work for a sin.

steps.title: Where is the verse for שליחות יד?
steps.stepSummary: We already know the source for מעילה. The גמרא asks where the Torah teaches that a שליח works for שליחות יד.
steps.simpleTranslation: מעילה is what we already said. What is the source for שליחות יד?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source of the second case it just mentioned. This sets up the ברייתא that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The source for מעילה was already given (the link to תרומה). But the claim of 'two verses' only works if there is also a verse showing that a שליח works for שליחות יד. The גמרא now asks for that verse.

keyTerms.meaning: A person guarding someone else's item

phrases.english: Misuse — that is what we said.
Misappropriation of a deposit, what is it?

steps.triggerLanguage: מְעִילָה הָא דַּאֲמַרַן שְׁלִיחוּת יָד מַאי הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the second case mentioned in Step 16
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The Torah source showing that a שליח works for שליחות יד

steps.title: The ברייתא: בית שמאי and בית הלל on 'על כל דבר פשע'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא. בית שמאי say a שומר is liable even for planning to take the item. בית הלל say he is liable only once he actually takes it.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: 'For every matter of trespass.' בית שמאי say this makes him liable for the thought just like the action. בית הלל say he is not liable until he actually takes it, as it says: 'If he did not put his hand...'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question by quoting a ברייתא about the פסוקים of שליחות יד. First the ברייתא gives the two opinions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית שמאי use the word 'כל' in 'על כל דבר פשע' to add liability for just thinking about or planning to take the item. בית הלל use the פסוק 'אם לא שלח ידו' to require an actual act. The ברייתא will soon show how 'על כל דבר פשע' teaches the case of a שליח.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught in a ברייתא

phrases.english: As it was taught: 'For every matter of trespass,'
Beit Shammai say:
to make him liable for the thought like the action.
And Beit Hillel say:

phrases.aramaic: אֵינוֹ חַיָּיב עַד שֶׁיִּשְׁלַח בּוֹ יָד,
phrases.english: He is not liable until he actually takes it,
as it is stated: 'If he did not put his hand, etc.'

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא עַל כׇּל דְּבַר פֶּשַׁע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts answering the question of Step 17 by quoting a ברייתא
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The source lies in the ברייתא about 'על כל דבר פשע', which is about to be explained

steps.title: בית שמאי challenge בית הלל from 'על כל דבר פשע'
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי ask בית הלל: doesn't the פסוק say 'על כל דבר פשע', which suggests liability even without an act?
steps.simpleTranslation: בית שמאי said to בית הלל: But doesn't it say 'For every matter of trespass'!
steps.whatsHappening: The debate in the ברייתא begins. בית שמאי challenge בית הלל with their פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית שמאי argue that the word 'כל' (every) widens liability to include even a plan to take the item. To them, requiring an actual act ignores this word.

keyTerms.meaning: But doesn't it say...? (a challenge from a פסוק)
Every, all. A word that includes more cases.

phrases.english: Beit Shammai said to Beit Hillel:
But isn't it stated: 'For every matter of trespass'!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ בֵּית שַׁמַּאי לְבֵית הִלֵּל וַהֲלֹא נֶאֱמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: בית שמאי challenge the opinion of בית הלל from Step 18
steps.kashyaTarget: בית הלל's view that an actual act is needed
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word 'כל' seems to make even a plan enough for liability

steps.title: בית הלל answer from 'אם לא שלח ידו'
steps.stepSummary: בית הלל answer with their own פסוק: 'אם לא שלח ידו במלאכת רעהו', which speaks of an actual act.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית הלל said to בית שמאי: But doesn't it say 'If he did not put his hand to his neighbor's property'!
steps.whatsHappening: בית הלל answer by pointing to their own פסוק. It clearly speaks about actually taking the item.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'שלח ידו' (put his hand) describe a physical act. So בית הלל say liability needs a real act, not just a plan.

keyTerms.meaning: Put out his hand. Actually took the item.

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרוּ לָהֶם בֵּית הִלֵּל לְבֵית שַׁמַּאי:
phrases.english: Beit Hillel said to Beit Shammai:

phrases.aramaic: וַהֲלֹא נֶאֱמַר ״אִם לֹא שָׁלַח יָדוֹ בִּמְלֶאכֶת רֵעֵהוּ״!
phrases.english: But isn't it stated: 'If he did not put his hand to his neighbor's property'!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לָהֶם בֵּית הִלֵּל לְבֵית שַׁמַּאי וַהֲלֹא נֶאֱמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: בית הלל respond to the challenge of Step 19
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'על כל דבר פשע' makes a plan enough
steps.terutzMaskana: 'שלח ידו' shows that a real act is needed

steps.title: Then why do we need 'על כל דבר פשע'?
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי ask: if an act is needed, what does the פסוק 'על כל דבר פשע' come to teach?
steps.simpleTranslation: בית שמאי said to בית הלל: If so, why do I need 'For every matter of trespass'?
steps.whatsHappening: בית שמאי push back. If בית הלל are right, the words 'על כל דבר פשע' seem to have no purpose.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every word of the Torah must teach something. If בית הלל don't use 'כל' to include a plan, they need to explain what it does teach. The answer will give us the source for a שליח in שליחות יד.

keyTerms.meaning: Why do I need it? What does it teach?

phrases.english: Beit Shammai said to Beit Hillel:

phrases.aramaic: אִם כֵּן, ״עַל כׇּל דְּבַר פֶּשַׁע״ לְמָה לִי?
phrases.english: If so, why do I need 'For every matter of trespass'?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם כֵּן עַל כׇּל דְּבַר פֶּשַׁע לְמָה לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: בית שמאי challenge בית הלל's answer from Step 20
steps.kashyaTarget: בית הלל's reading of the פסוקים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If an act is required, the words 'על כל דבר פשע' would teach nothing

steps.title: 'על כל דבר פשע' teaches liability through a slave or שליח
steps.stepSummary: בית הלל answer that 'על כל דבר פשע' teaches that the שומר is liable even if he told his slave or שליח to take the item. This is the source for שליחות יד.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because I might think I only know the case where he took it himself. If he told his slave or his שליח, from where do we know? The פסוק says: 'For every matter of trespass.'
steps.whatsHappening: בית הלל explain what 'על כל דבר פשע' teaches. This answers the question of Step 17 and shows where the source for שליחות יד is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'כל' adds the case where the שומר sends someone else to take the item. So in שליחות יד a שליח works even though it is a sin. This is the second verse alongside מעילה, which is why they are 'two verses that come as one'.
steps.whatToRemember: The Torah tells us twice that a שליח works for a sin: once by מעילה and once by שליחות יד ('על כל דבר פשע'). Because it was said twice, these are 'two verses that come as one'. They stay exceptions, and the general rule of אין שליח לדבר עבירה still stands.

phrases.english: For one might think I only know of him himself;
phrases.notes: This is בית הלל answering. He means the שומר who took the item with his own hands.

phrases.english: if he told his slave or his agent, from where do we know?
The verse states: 'For every matter of trespass.'

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁיָּכוֹל אֵין לִי אֶלָּא הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers בית שמאי's question of Step 21, and so completes the answer to Step 17
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reassigns the verse to a new teaching
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'על כל דבר פשע' seemed to have no purpose for בית הלל
steps.terutzMaskana: It teaches that the שומר is liable when his slave or שליח takes the item
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the second verse that, together with מעילה, blocks us from learning that a שליח works for every sin.

steps.title: This works for בית הלל, but what about בית שמאי?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that the source for שליחות יד done through an agent fits בית הלל. It then begins to ask about בית שמאי, who use that פסוק for a different lesson: that thought counts like action.
steps.simpleTranslation: This works well for בית הלל. But according to בית שמאי, who use this פסוק to teach that thinking about it counts like doing it...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a new question. It agrees that the source from step 22 works for בית הלל, then turns to בית שמאי, and the question is completed in the next line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 22, בית הלל used 'על כל דבר פשע' to teach that a שומר is liable even when his slave or שליח takes the item. בית שמאי cannot use the פסוק for that, because they already need it to teach that a plan to take the item makes him liable, which is מחשבה כמעשה. So for בית שמאי, the rule about sending someone else seems to have no source.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It works out well': this fits one opinion, and a 'but' usually follows about another opinion
Who establish it: who apply the פסוק to a specific lesson
Thought counts like action: just planning to take the item makes the שומר liable

steps.confusionAlert: This line is not the whole question. The גמרא only names the problem here, that בית שמאי have 'used up' the פסוק. The actual question, 'so where does their source come from?', comes in the next line.

phrases.english: This works out well according to בית הלל.
phrases.notes: He means the source from step 22: for בית הלל, 'על כל דבר פשע' teaches liability when a slave or שליח takes the item.

phrases.english: But according to בית שמאי,
who apply this verse
to teach that thought is like action,

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנִיחָא לְבֵית הִלֵּל. אֶלָּא לְבֵית שַׁמַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the answer of step 22 for בית הלל and begins to challenge whether it works for בית שמאי.
steps.kashyaTarget: The source for שליחות יד done through a slave or שליח, according to בית שמאי.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: בית שמאי already use 'על כל דבר פשע' to teach מחשבה כמעשה, so the פסוק is not free to teach liability through an agent. Their view seems to be missing a source.
